html:
The constitution of Kazakhstan adopted by referendum on 30 August 1995 made the country a strongly presidential republic. It replaced the first post-Soviet constitution of 1993, and it stayed the basic law until a new constitution took effect on 1 July 2026.

It was written under President Nursultan Nazarbayev, who had dissolved parliament earlier in 1995 and ruled by decree. It gave the president power to appoint the government, issue decrees with the force of law and dissolve parliament, which became a body of two chambers. It declared Kazakhstan a secular, unitary state, with Kazakh as the state language and Russian "officially used on equal grounds", a key promise to the large Russian minority.

Amendments in 2007 let Nazarbayev, as First President, stand for office without term limits. After the unrest of January 2022, a referendum under his successor Kassym-Jomart Tokayev cut presidential powers and removed Nazarbayev's special status. In March 2026 voters approved a new constitution. Under the 1995 text the capital moved to Astana in 1997.
